rcPflichtenP.zur_ausbildung_gehoeren_nicht_nur: Training is not only about rights. The Vocational Training Act lists what you are obliged to do as a trainee:

rcPflichtenL.die_aufgaben_die_dir_im: carry out the tasks assigned to you as part of your training carefully
rcPflichtenL.an_der_berufsschule_an_pruefungen: attend vocational school, exams and courses for which you are released
rcPflichtenL.weisungen_folgen_die_dir_im: follow instructions given to you as part of your training
rcPflichtenL.die_ordnung_der_ausbildungsstaette_beach: observe the rules of the training workplace, such as health and safety and house rules
rcPflichtenL.werkzeug_maschinen_und_einrichtungen_pfl: treat tools, machines and equipment with care
rcPflichtenL.ueber_betriebs_und_geschaeftsgeheimnisse: keep business and trade secrets confidential
rcPflichtenL.einen_schriftlichen_oder_elektronischen_: keep a written or electronic training record, i.e. the training log

rcPflichtenP2.die_pflichten_des_betriebs_stehen: The company’s duties are set out in Section 14 BBiG: it must train you so that you can reach the training goal, provide training materials free of charge and only give you tasks that serve the purpose of your training.

rcKuendP.in_der_probezeit_koennen_beide: During the probationary period either side can terminate at any time without notice and without giving a reason. After that, the company may only terminate without notice for good cause, in writing and stating the reasons, and within two weeks of learning of the reason (Section 22 BBiG). After the probationary period there is no ordinary termination by the company. You yourself can terminate with four weeks’ notice if you give up the training or want to train for a different occupation.

rcUrlaubP.fuer_minderjaehrige_gilt_das_jugendarbei: For minors the Youth Employment Protection Act applies: at least 30 working days if you are not yet 16 at the start of the calendar year, 27 working days under 17 and 25 working days under 18 (Section 19 JArbSchG). Adult trainees are entitled to at least 24 working days under the Federal Leave Act, i.e. 20 days with a five-day week (Section 3 BUrlG). Many collective and training agreements give more.

faq.name: Can my boss do that? – Apprentice Rights Checker
faq.description: Interactive rights checker for trainees and apprentices in Germany, with scenarios on overtime, holiday, dismissal, vocational school and more.

mainEntity.name: Can my boss order me to work overtime as an apprentice?

acceptedAnswer.text: As a rule, no. Apprentices who are minors may work a maximum of 8 hours/day and 40 hours/week (§ 8 JArbSchG). For apprentices of legal age, the Working Hours Act applies. Overtime must be paid or compensated with time off (§ 17 (3) BBiG).

mainEntity.name: Can my boss cancel my holiday as an apprentice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Once approved, holiday can only be revoked in absolute exceptional cases. Apprentices who are minors are entitled to 25–30 working days/year (§ 19 JArbSchG), adults at least 24 working days (§ 3 BUrlG).

mainEntity.name: Do I have to clean and sweep the hall as an apprentice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only in moderation. Apprentices may only be assigned tasks that serve the purpose of the training (§ 14 BBiG). Occasionally tidying your own workstation is fine; regularly cleaning the company is an impermissible non-training activity.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to go in to work after vocational school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apprentices who are minors with more than 5 lessons on a single day are fully released (§ 9 JArbSchG). Vocational-school time counts towards working time (§ 15 BBiG).

mainEntity.name: Can my boss dismiss me as an apprentice after the probationary period?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only for good cause and without notice (§ 22 BBiG). Ordinary termination by the company is not possible after the probationary period. A warning is usually required beforehand.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to use my holiday for the exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: No! You have a statutory right to paid release for exams and the day before (§ 15 BBiG). This may not be credited against your holiday.

mainEntity.name: Does my trainer have to provide tools and work materials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The training company is obliged to provide training materials free of charge – tools, materials, specialist books and any prescribed work clothing (§ 14 (1) no. 3 BBiG).
